issues.body: The README calls `--check` the reproducibility gate and says it enforces byte identity, snapshot agreement, unknown-family rejection, and related-work/metric guards, but this PR only adds the command and documentation. There is no test or CI invocation of it anywhere in the checkout. Thus all load-bearing guarantees depend on a contributor remembering to run the script manually; stale or hand-edited generated artifacts and an unclassified new snapshot member can merge undetected. The script passes when invoked now, but that does not make the regression protection non-vacuous.
issues.fix_hint: Add an automated repository test or CI/docs-quality step that runs `bench/zk-compose/scripts/constraint_pack.py --check`, and ensure that gate runs when the snapshot, generator, or either generated artifact changes.
issues.title: The reproducibility check is not wired into an automated gate

verdict.summary: The generator currently reproduces both committed artifacts and its snapshot joins are internally consistent, and the ZK/security caveats are appropriately explicit. However, the new anti-drift and reproducibility guarantees are only implemented as an opt-in command: no test or CI gate in the diff invokes `constraint_pack.py --check`. Consequently the claimed fail-closed coverage and byte-identity acceptance criterion can silently regress or the generated artifacts can become stale without any repository gate failing.
